subsystems.name: Trait target genes
subsystems.role: the plant genes that control the signals pollinators use to find flowers.
parts: nectar secretion and sugar composition genes

subsystems.name: Gene editing toolkit
subsystems.role: makes precise changes in those genes without leaving foreign DNA.
parts: guide RNAs targeted to chosen sequences

subsystems.name: Plant transformation and regeneration
subsystems.role: gets the editing tools into the plant and grows a whole new plant from edited cells.

subsystems.name: Pollinator sensing and behaviour
subsystems.role: defines what a given pollinator species can see, smell and learn.

subsystems.name: Field testing and monitoring
subsystems.role: checks whether edited traits actually attract pollinators and raise yield under real conditions.
parts: pollinator counts and pollen transfer measurements

buildSteps.title: Map the interaction
buildSteps.detail: Study which floral cues a target pollinator uses — colour, scent, nectar volume — and which plant genes control them.

buildSteps.title: Choose and edit genes
buildSteps.detail: Design CRISPR guides to tweak those genes, aiming for stronger or more specific signals without harming the plant.

buildSteps.title: Transform plant cells
buildSteps.detail: Deliver the editing tools into cells of a crop variety, then regenerate whole plants from the edited tissue.

buildSteps.title: Screen in the greenhouse
buildSteps.detail: Grow the edited lines and measure the changed trait — colour, scent profile, nectar output — against unedited controls.

buildSteps.title: Test with pollinators
buildSteps.detail: Present edited and control flowers to the target pollinator in cages or flight tunnels and record visits.

buildSteps.title: Run confined field trials
buildSteps.detail: Plant edited lines in isolated plots, track pollinator visits and measure fruit or seed yield over a season.

buildSteps.title: Breed into elite varieties
buildSteps.detail: Cross the edited trait into high-yielding commercial lines, selecting for both the trait and crop performance.

buildSteps.title: Navigate regulation
buildSteps.detail: Depending on the country, gene-edited crops may need approval as genetically modified organisms or may be treated like conventional breeding.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Release seed to farmers where approved, then watch whether the intended pollinators actually increase and whether yields become more stable.

prerequisites.why: already used in research and some commercial crops, but not yet for pollination traits.
many major crops remain hard to edit because regenerating a whole plant from edited cells is unreliable.
we know a lot about honeybees and some wild bees, but far less about many tropical and specialist pollinators.
rules differ widely by country, and approval for a pollination-focused trait would be a new case.
baseline data on pollinator populations are patchy, making it hard to prove an edited crop helped.

pathway.milestone: laboratory research identifying genes for floral colour, scent and nectar in model plants
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of candidate edits that could influence pollinator behaviour.

pathway.milestone: greenhouse and small-scale field trials of edited flowers with controlled pollinator exposure
pathway.unlocks: evidence that an edit can change visitation rates without harming the plant.

pathway.milestone: regulatory decisions on gene-edited crops with ecological traits
pathway.unlocks: a clear route to test and release such varieties in at least some countries.

pathway.milestone: edited crop varieties deployed in pollinator-dependent farming regions
pathway.unlocks: more stable yields where wild pollinators are declining, if the approach proves effective and safe.
